modkeel.button.tooltip: Your worlds, your mods and lag spikes
modkeel.crash.title: The game closed because of an error
modkeel.kind.mixin_failed: A mod could not change the game's code. Usually it is made for another Minecraft version, or two mods change the same code.
modkeel.kind.missing_class: A mod used code this game does not have. Usually it is made for another version of Minecraft, of the loader or of a library.
modkeel.kind.out_of_memory: The game ran out of memory. Give Minecraft more RAM in your launcher, or remove heavy mods.
modkeel.kind.generic: The game stopped with an error.
modkeel.share.tooltip: Anonymous. Helps find the fix that works for most players.
modkeel.share.note: Sent with the fix you pick, and later whether it held (play time, and whether the crash came back). No names, file paths or logs.
modkeel.sessions.tooltip: Anonymous: play time, lag spikes and the mods behind them. Turn it off in Modkeel > Settings.
modkeel.sessions.note: Sent when the game starts next: minutes in a world, whether it crashed, the 20 worst lag spikes and the mods behind them, and the mod list once per set. No names, file paths or logs.
modkeel.sent.mods: Your %s mods: name, version and a fingerprint of each file
modkeel.sent.mods_bundled: Your %1$s mods and the %2$s bundled in them: name, version and a fingerprint of each file
modkeel.sent.mods_known: Your mod list: already sent for these mods
modkeel.sent.frames: Where it happened: %s lines of code names
modkeel.sent.fix_disable: The fix you picked: turn off %s
modkeel.sent.fix_revert: The fix you picked: go back to the mods that worked
modkeel.sent.minutes: %s minutes in a world, %s of them playing
modkeel.sent.not_crashed: That the game did not crash
modkeel.sent.spikes: %s lag spikes and the mods behind them
modkeel.sent.activity: How much you used each mod (%s mods)
modkeel.sent.install: A random number for this game, so repeats count once
modkeel.revert.none: Nothing to go back to yet: Modkeel remembers your mods after 10 minutes of play without a crash.
modkeel.revert.confirm_title: Go back to the mods that worked?
modkeel.disable.dependents: These mods need it and will stop loading too: %s
modkeel.restart_note: Minecraft will close to apply this. Start it again from your launcher.
modkeel.health.title: Modkeel
modkeel.restore.confirm_title: Go back to the copy from %s?
modkeel.welcome.title: Modkeel Companion
modkeel.welcome.intro: A safety net for modded Minecraft. Nothing to set up.
modkeel.welcome.backup: Backs up your worlds before they load with different mods.
modkeel.welcome.crash: After a crash, shows which mod caused it and fixes it in one click. Every fix can be undone.
modkeel.welcome.good: Remembers the last set of mods that worked, so you can always go back.
modkeel.welcome.privacy: Nothing is sent unless you choose "Help other players".
modkeel.welcome.later: All of this is under the Modkeel button on the title screen.
modkeel.outcome.open: watching (%s h %s min played so far)
modkeel.outcome.held_1h: held for over an hour of play (%s h %s min)
modkeel.outcome.held_5h: held for over 5 hours of play: it worked
modkeel.lab.title: Modkeel lab, Minecraft %s
modkeel.lab.crashes: %s: this exact file crashed on Minecraft %s in our lab.
modkeel.lab.clash: %s and %s clashed when run together in our lab.
modkeel.lab.verified: %s of %s mods ran in our lab on this version, as these exact files: %s
modkeel.lab.other_version: The file names of these mods point at another Minecraft version: %s
modkeel.crash.later: Nothing changes. This stays under the Modkeel button until you close Minecraft.
modkeel.health.crash: The last launch closed with an error
modkeel.health.last_fail: Some files could not be changed: close Minecraft fully and start it again.
modkeel.health.turned_off: It was made for another Minecraft version: Forge could not read it and would have closed the game before it started. You can turn it back on from Mods, but it will be turned off again while it stops the game.
modkeel.health.clash_body: Both include the same piece of code, and the game won't start with both. Modkeel turned off %s so you could play.
modkeel.health.clash_game_body: It includes a piece of code the game already has, and the game won't start with it. Modkeel turned it off so you could play.
modkeel.health.clash_swap_note: %s will be turned off. Minecraft closes to apply this; start it again from your launcher.
modkeel.health.clash_details: Both contain the Java package %s. Java won't load two copies of one package, so the game would close before loading any mod. Usually two mods bundle the same library; their authors can fix it by relocating it.
modkeel.cta: Modkeel can look for versions of your mods that work together today: modkeel.com
modkeel.action.reverted: Went back to the last good mod set
modkeel.reason.load_failed: the loader says it failed to load
modkeel.reason.mixin_trace: its mixin code is in the error
modkeel.reason.trace: its code is in the error
modkeel.reason.version: another mod expects a different version of it
modkeel.reason.lab_crashes: this exact file crashed on Minecraft %s in the Modkeel lab
modkeel.reason.file_name: its file name says it is for Minecraft %s, not %s
modkeel.reason.lab_clash: the Modkeel lab saw it clash with %s
modkeel.lab.none: None of your %s mods tested on this version yet.
modkeel.spikes.tooltip: Which mod was running during each freeze in this session
modkeel.spikes.title: Modkeel: lag spikes
modkeel.spikes.intro: Freezes longer than %s s in this session, and whose code was running during each one.
modkeel.spikes.none: No lag spikes so far. Modkeel keeps watching while you play.
modkeel.spikes.other_programs: Other programs were using the processor
modkeel.spikes.gc_hint: Java memory cleanup caused some of these. Giving Minecraft more RAM in your launcher often helps.
modkeel.spikes.gpu_hint: Some froze waiting on the graphics card: lower the render distance, or check that Minecraft uses your dedicated graphics card.
modkeel.health.pill_same: Same as when it all worked
modkeel.crash.unclear: It is not clear which mod it was
modkeel.crash.changed: You changed %s mods since everything last worked.
modkeel.crash.unchanged: No mod changed since everything last worked.
modkeel.crash.fix_revert: Go back to the mods that worked
modkeel.rescue.title: Your world is safe
modkeel.rescue.saved: %s was saved when the game closed.
modkeel.rescue.saved_min: %s was saved %s min before the error: you only lose that.
modkeel.rescue.copy: There is also a copy from %s.
modkeel.more.title: More options
modkeel.more.revert: Go back to the mods that worked
modkeel.more.revert_text: The last ones you played with without problems. Turns off %s new or changed mods.
modkeel.more.other_text: If you think it was another one that shows up in the error.
modkeel.more.report_text: Minecraft's own file, useful when asking the mod's author for help.
modkeel.disable.points:
· Minecraft closes; open it again from your launcher.
· The mod is turned off, not deleted.
· Turn it back on from the Modkeel button.
modkeel.revert.points:
· These new or changed mods are turned off: %s
· Mods you removed since then come back.
· Minecraft closes; open it again from your launcher.
modkeel.restore.points:
· You lose what you did in %s after that copy.
· The world as it is now is kept aside in modkeel/replaced: nothing is deleted.
modkeel.home.worlds_none: No copies yet. Modkeel copies a world before it loads with changed mods.
modkeel.home.mods_same: Mods: %s. Same as when it all worked.
modkeel.settings.alerts: A notice when the game freezes
modkeel.world.keep: Modkeel keeps the %s most recent copies of each world.
modkeel.starting.title: Modkeel: Minecraft could not start
modkeel.starting.text:
%s stopped Minecraft from starting last time, and will likely do it again.

Disable it and close the game? Then start it again.
You can turn it back on from Modkeel.
modkeel.gpu.toast: Open Modkeel on the title screen to see why
modkeel.gpu.unused_title: Minecraft is using the slower graphics
modkeel.gpu.unused_text: It draws on %1$s, built into the processor. This computer has the %2$s driver installed, so it most likely has a faster %2$s card that Minecraft is not using.
modkeel.gpu.software_title: Minecraft is drawing without a graphics driver
modkeel.gpu.software_text: It draws with %s, which uses the processor and runs games very slowly. Install the driver from your graphics card or computer maker's website.
modkeel.gpu.switch_hint: Modkeel can switch it for you.
modkeel.gpu.switch_text: Modkeel will set this Java to High performance in Windows (Settings > System > Display > Graphics), as you could do by hand. It applies the next time Minecraft starts.
modkeel.gpu.switched: Done. Close Minecraft and start it again to play on the %s card.
modkeel.gpu.still: Windows was already asked to use the %1$s card, but Minecraft still draws on the integrated graphics. Your launcher may start a different Java, or the %1$s control panel may override it: choose the %1$s card for Minecraft's Java there.
modkeel.gpu.switch_failed_title: Windows did not accept the change
modkeel.gpu.switch_failed: Set it by hand: Settings > System > Display > Graphics, add %s and choose High performance.
modkeel.gpu.linux_nvidia: To use it, start Minecraft with __NV_PRIME_RENDER_OFFLOAD=1 __GLX_VENDOR_LIBRARY_NAME=nvidia (environment variables, in your launcher's settings).
modkeel.gpu.linux_amd: To use it, start Minecraft with DRI_PRIME=1 (an environment variable, in your launcher's settings).
modkeel.mem.low_title: Minecraft has little memory for this pack
modkeel.mem.low_text: Java can use %s GB. With %s mods, %s GB keeps the game from stuttering or running out of memory.
modkeel.mem.high_title: Minecraft takes almost all of the computer's memory
modkeel.mem.high_text: Java can use %s GB of the computer's %s GB, so the system starts using the disk and everything stutters. %s GB is plenty for this pack.
modkeel.mem.bits32_text: 32-bit Java can't use more than about 1.5 GB, too little for mods. Install 64-bit Java, or let your launcher use its own.
modkeel.mem.how_prism: In Prism: Edit the instance > Settings > Java > Maximum memory allocation: %s MiB. Then restart Minecraft.
modkeel.mem.how_curseforge: In CurseForge: Settings > Minecraft > Java Settings > Allocated Memory: %s MB. Then restart Minecraft.
modkeel.mem.how_modrinth: In the Modrinth App: the instance's Settings > Java and memory > Memory allocated: %s MB. Then restart Minecraft.
modkeel.mem.how_vanilla: In the Minecraft Launcher: Installations > Edit > More options > JVM arguments: change -Xmx… to -Xmx%sG. Then restart Minecraft.
modkeel.mem.how_other: In your launcher's settings for this game, set the maximum memory to %s GB. Then restart Minecraft.
